seen_animation: A black line drawing of a cello stands in the center of the frame with its scroll at the top and its body cropped by the bottom edge; grey scenery around it shows a dark panel outline at top left, a music stand and stacked boxes at left, a head-and-shoulders outline behind the cello, and a rectangle with small shapes and another head outline at right. In frames 1-4 the neck leans to the right with the scroll near the top right of center. Across frames 5-16 the cello slowly rotates toward upright and slides slightly left and down, so by frame 16 the neck is closer to vertical and the body sits a little lower and further left. The strings, the bridge/f-hole mark and the waist notches stay attached to the body in every frame. The scenery does not move. These are still frames only, not playback.
seen_film: A cellist in a red dress plays a cello in a rehearsal room, with a seated audience at the sides, a music stand and chair at left, and a dark screen at top left. The cello's scroll is right of center near the top. In frames 1-4 her left hand is high on the neck and her head is bowed; through frames 5-12 her left hand moves down the fingerboard and her bow arm swings across; in frames 13-16 she leans and turns her head, the bow is visible at the lower right, and the cello neck has become more upright and shifted slightly left compared with frame 1.
named_subject: a cello (the instrument, without the player)
evidence: Frame 1 animation scroll sits at about the same position as the film's scroll in frame 1 (upper right of center, neck leaning right). Frames 5-12 show the neck gradually straightening in small even steps, matching the film's gradual change in cello angle over the same frames. Frames 13-16 show the most upright neck and the body shifted left and lower, as in film frames 13-16. No frame shows a second outline, a missing part, or a sudden change in shape; the scenery (screen at top left, music stand at left, person outline behind) is placed where those objects are in the film.
primary_gap: The motion is a slow rigid tilt only, so the film's playing action (the hand moving down the fingerboard and the bow stroke in frames 13-16) has no trace in the animated character.
closes_when: Small vibrations or a slight rocking of the cello body in time with the film's bowing, and a bow line appearing at the lower right in frames 13-16 where the film's bow is visible, drawn in the same thin wobbly stroke as the doodle.
protect: The doodle's construction: the round looped scroll, the narrow neck with doubled string lines, the notched waist, the single angular bridge/f-hole mark; the consistent stroke weight; the even, gradual tilt from frame 1 to 16; the placement of the scroll and body matching the film frame by frame; the static grey scenery.
identity_gap: The cello is the doodle's drawing enlarged and tilted with its scroll, doubled strings, notched waist and bridge mark intact, though the lower body is cut off by the frame edge so the doodle's rounded base is never seen.
